chunks: What the Shaykh informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from al-Nawfalī, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: “There is no wudu (ablution) from something trodden underfoot.”
Al-Nawfalī said: He means that which you tread upon with your foot.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing performed for acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does stepping on something with your foot invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling related to taharah and wudu (ablution), stating that stepping on something with the foot does not itself necessitate wudu. The explanatory note clarifies that the statement refers to whatever is trodden upon underfoot, indicating a jurisprudential principle in ritual purity.
